test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 3 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Employee's State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) does NOT provide social security in respect of medical benefits to the employees of:
solution:
The correct answer is **Multinational Corporations.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Government Sector: True. Generally, employees working in the government sector are not covered under the ESIC scheme because the government has its health care and employee welfare schemes. Government employees benefit from **different health insurance and medical schemes specifically designed for them.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Private Sector: **False. The ESIC scheme very much includes employees in the private sector, provided the establishment meets the criteria set by **ESIC in terms of the number of employees and the nature of the business, among other factors.**
 
• **Multinational Corporations (MNCs): **False. Employees working in MNCs that operate in India and fall within the employee threshold as stipulated by **ESIC regulations are covered under the ESIC scheme.**
 
• The key determinant is not the multinational nature but rather compliance with ESIC eligibility criteria.
 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs):** False. Employees of Public Sector Undertakings can be covered under ESIC, depending on the specific terms and conditions governing their employment and the applicability of ESIC regulations to the undertaking.
 
• Like in the private sector, compliance with **ESIC criteria is the key determinant.**
